The smallest possible value of a+b+c is 79.

Multiply the equation by 1001 = 7·11·13, which is the least common denominator of 77, 91 and 143. This gives

13a + 11b + 7c = 1001.

Let S = a + b + c. Then 13S = 13a + 13b + 13c = (1001 − 11b − 7c) + 13b + 13c = 1001 + 2b + 6c, so

S = 77 + (2b + 6c)/13.

Since S is an integer and 13 is odd, 13 must divide b + 3c. Write b + 3c = 13k, which gives S = 77 + 2k. Because b and c are positive, b + 3c ≥ 4, so k ≥ 1.

Try k = 1, so b + 3c = 13. Take c = 1 and b = 10. Then

a = (1001 − 110 − 7)/13 = 884/13 = 68,

which is a positive integer. The sum is 68 + 10 + 1 = 79.

Check: 68/77 + 10/91 + 1/143 = (884 + 110 + 7)/1001 = 1001/1001 = 1.

Since k = 1 gives the minimum S = 77 + 2 = 79 and it is attained, this is the smallest value.

ANSWER: 79
